# Therapist Web Design (therapistweb.design)

> A small Denver studio building bespoke, hand-coded websites for therapists and counselors in private practice. No templates. No platform fees. No two sites alike.

## About

Therapist Web Design is operated by Chad Moravec, a web designer and developer based in Denver, CO. Chad's wife runs a group therapy practice, which means he understands the mental health private practice world from the inside: the directories, the niche specialties, the language that helps clients find and trust a therapist online.

Every site is hand-coded from scratch. No WordPress, no page builders, no themes. The result is a fast, secure, uniquely designed website the client owns outright: domain, hosting, and code all in their name.

## Services

- **[Custom website design](https://therapistweb.design/services/website-design/)** for solo and group therapy practices (nationwide): Solo from $2,800, Group from $4,200
- **[Group practice websites](https://therapistweb.design/services/group-practice/)**: up to 4 additional clinician profiles with individual schema markup, $4,200
- **[Blog / Journal setup](https://therapistweb.design/services/blog-journal/)**: self-service posting, $850 add-on to either package
- **[SEO](https://therapistweb.design/services/seo/)**: schema.org markup, sitemaps, llms.txt, and Google Business Profile setup, built in from day one
- **Website refreshes & platform migrations** for practices on existing platforms (WordPress, Squarespace, Wix)
- Also: **web applications** (client portals, booking systems, internal tools) via [Studio Null](https://studionull.io)

Pricing is published, not quoted blind: Solo practice $2,800 (homepage, about, a dedicated page per service or specialty each SEO-targeted to the practice area, FAQ, privacy policy, terms & conditions, contact). Group practice $4,200 (Solo + up to 4 clinician profiles). Blog/Journal add-on +$850. Add-ons: SEO/authority carryover for migrations from $250, branded email templates from $200, TinaCMS self-edit access from $400, Google Business Profile setup included free with new Solo/Group builds ($200 standalone for an existing site). Everything else billed at $150/hr. See [full pricing](https://therapistweb.design/pricing/).

## Questions clients ask

- **HIPAA:** The sites have no database and hold no client records. The contact form is where HIPAA applies, so each build uses either a minimal form that asks visitors not to share clinical details, or a form routed through a service that signs a Business Associate Agreement (often the practice's EHR contact widget). See [the HIPAA contact form article](https://therapistweb.design/journal/is-your-therapy-website-contact-form-hipaa-compliant/).
- **After launch:** The first 30 days of questions and fixes are included. After that, changes are $150 an hour, billed only when requested. No required maintenance plan; nothing renews.
- **If the developer disappears:** The domain, hosting and code repository are in the client's name from day one, and each site is plain HTML and CSS with documentation that any web developer can pick up.
- **Reviews:** Five 5-star reviews on the [Therapist Web Design Google Business Profile](https://g.page/r/CeDcbTy7Xp7oEBM), from therapists including Shayla Martinez-O'Brien (Golden Hour Wellness), Whitney Lovett (Lovett Counseling & Consulting) and Leslie Cedar.
- **Contact:** hello@therapistweb.design, call or text (720) 466-1013, or book a free 30-minute intro call at https://calendly.com/chad-m-moravec/intro-call.

## Journal articles

- [Is the contact form on your therapy website HIPAA compliant?](https://therapistweb.design/journal/is-your-therapy-website-contact-form-hipaa-compliant/): Why a therapy website's contact form, not the site itself, is where HIPAA applies; what counts as protected health information from a prospective client; the two form setups (a minimal form that steers clinical details elsewhere, or a form through a BAA-covered service such as an EHR widget); the 2024 court ruling on analytics tracking; and a five-minute self-check.
- [What Google, and ChatGPT, actually see when they look at your site](https://therapistweb.design/journal/what-search-engines-and-ai-actually-see-on-your-site/): Plain-English explanation of meta titles/descriptions, schema markup, canonical tags, sitemap.xml, and llms.txt, and what each one actually does.
- [How to tell if your website looks AI-generated](https://therapistweb.design/journal/how-to-tell-if-your-website-looks-ai-generated/): The visual tells of AI-generated or templated design (gradients, fonts, button shapes, stock photography) and why they cost a therapy practice more trust than most other businesses.
- [Do you need a blog on your therapy website?](https://therapistweb.design/journal/do-you-need-a-blog-on-your-therapy-website/): Honest pros and cons of a therapist blog, who should have one, and how to keep a site without a blog current in Google's eyes (service pages, accurate facts, FAQ, Google Business Profile, honest lastmod dates, Search Console).
- [I Googled myself, so you don't have to](https://therapistweb.design/journal/i-googled-myself-so-you-dont-have-to/): What actually shows up when you Google your own practice name, including what Google's AI Mode says, why that matters, and what to check for your own practice.
- [What's actually included in a therapist website package?](https://therapistweb.design/journal/what-a-therapist-website-package-includes/): A plain breakdown of what's in the Solo and Group packages, what's a paid add-on, and what still gets billed hourly.
- [When you need a web app, not a website](https://therapistweb.design/journal/when-you-need-a-web-app-not-a-website/): The actual difference between a website and a web application, examples (client portals, booking systems, internal tools), and where that work happens (Studio Null).
- [The real cost of renting your therapy website](https://therapistweb.design/journal/renting-vs-owning-your-therapy-website/): The math and ownership case for a one-time hand-coded site vs. subscription platforms like Brighter Vision, TherapySites, or Squarespace.
- [How clients actually find a therapist online](https://therapistweb.design/journal/how-clients-find-a-therapist-online/): How directories, Google, and word of mouth work together, and the job a therapist's own website does in that chain.
- [How much does a therapist website cost?](https://therapistweb.design/journal/how-much-does-a-therapist-website-cost/): The DIY vs. template-designer vs. custom-build cost landscape and what drives the price.
- [Is Psychology Today enough, or do you need your own website?](https://therapistweb.design/journal/psychology-today-vs-your-own-website/): Why a directory profile and an owned website do different jobs, and why most therapists need both.

## Technical approach

All builds are static HTML/CSS/JS. No CMS runtime, no database, no server-side code. Sites are version-controlled in a GitHub repository owned by the client and deployed to edge hosting (Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages) for zero ongoing hosting fees. An optional lightweight editor (TinaCMS) can be added when a client wants to edit their own copy. Contact and intake forms are custom-built and fully branded via EmailJS, designed to match the site rather than a generic embed, so there is no server to maintain. Every build includes semantic HTML structure, local SEO targeting, JSON-LD structured data, an XML sitemap, and proper meta tags from day one, so both search engines and AI assistants can understand and recommend the practice.
